requirements.title: School transfer timing
requirements.summary: Traditional undergraduate external transfers enter in fall because of required-course sequences; internal transfers may enter any term. The separately named Computing and Security Technology rolling-admission exception is not an AI/ML exception.

requirements.title: Co-op completion
requirements.summary: Successful co-op completion is required for a co-op degree. AI/ML offers the one-co-op/four-year or three-co-op/five-year routes stated in its own degree catalog.

requirements.title: First-year design exceptions
requirements.summary: A complete design sequence from another Drexel college or prior institution can substitute for CI 101–103; a first design course can replace CI 101, leaving CI 102–103. Late major-changers unable to finish before junior/senior standing may replace up to six credits with CCI electives. Advising records listed exceptions in DegreeWorks; unlisted exceptions need written Associate Department Head approval. The AI/ML catalog’s explicit ENGR sequence alternative is retained independently.

requirements.title: Senior design registration and exceptions
requirements.summary: The school describes a thesis option in place of the team project but does not provide a finite thesis-course mapping here. Project groups continue across the sequence; group changes need instructor and coordinator permission. Trailer exceptions need Associate Department Head approval. These school rules do not silently replace the AI/ML catalog’s CI/ECE sequence choices.

requirements.title: UNIV 101 failure or withdrawal replacement
requirements.summary: From fall 2024, freshmen with F/W in fall and/or spring UNIV 101 cannot repeat it for credit: GPA at least 2.75 adds one free-elective credit; below 2.75 requires a GSTD 100/200-level course in the next active term. Advising must reconcile this one-credit replacement policy with the AI/ML catalog’s two-credit total UNIV CI101 allocation.

requirements.title: First-year design failures
requirements.summary: CI 101 failure requires a spring retake in the same academic year. CI 102 failure prevents the next CI 103 registration: repeat CI 102/103 in year-two fall/winter. CI 103 failure requires repeating it. Five-year fall/winter co-op students use the stated online sections.

requirements.title: Course substitutions and prerequisite waivers
requirements.summary: Submit written substitution and prerequisite-waiver requests to advising by the first day of term, with approval by the end of week one. Substitutions need case-specific advisor recommendation and ADH/program-director approval. A prerequisite waiver does not waive later completion of a required course; missing the deadline requires another way to meet the degree rule.

requirements.title: Independent-study limits
requirements.summary: Use a formal independent-study agreement through advising and a full-time college faculty supervisor. Do not duplicate an offered course; undergraduate independent-study credit toward graduation is capped at 12.

requirements.title: Graduate-course exceptions for non-BSMS undergraduates
requirements.summary: For CCI undergraduates outside an approved BSMS, graduate-course permission requires cumulative GPA at least 3.0, B or better major grades, and completed major core through pre-junior level. The course must serve the degree, lack an undergraduate equivalent, receive faculty and both graduate/undergraduate ADH approvals, and have space after graduate registration. Limit two courses; additional elective acceptance review and advising-maintained equivalence/approved lists apply.

requirements.title: Co-op registration, earned units and waivers
requirements.summary: Register employment by drop/add of the assigned quarter-cycle. Earn credit through successful work and Employment Summary and Planner completion during assigned co-op terms. Steinbright determines 16 Drexel Co-op Units per term; missing units must be made up unless the academic unit approves a degree-requirement waiver. DCUs are not course credits and are not added to the 180-credit academic minimum. The page’s separately marked fall-2027 semester timetable is prospective, not applied to this quarter plan.

requirements.title: Co-op eligibility
requirements.summary: Co-op eligibility requires a co-op concentration, completed preparation course, introduction/reflection meeting, active job search and advisor communication, progress toward graduation, cumulative GPA at least 2.0, and being on track for 24 credits over the prior two academic terms. Domestic work requires legal work authorization. For a preceding summer vacation use the prior winter/spring enrollment. Ineligibility receives case review/appeal and normally postpones co-op one year; repeated low-GPA/progress delays require a revised academic plan.

requirements.title: Co-op finalization
requirements.summary: Complete the ES&P in the final month and attend the return meeting with the co-op advisor. Failure can yield no co-op units, missing graduation requirements or loss of later co-op eligibility. Grade/registration changes are not considered more than one year after the final grade.

requirements.title: Graduating on co-op and future policy
requirements.summary: Under the current quarter policy, graduating at the end of a final co-op requires academic-advisor discussion and an approved plan reviewed by the co-op advisor. A separately announced rule effective fall 2027 forbids a final co-op term; it is recorded as prospective, not retrospectively applied to this 2026 quarter curriculum.
